existing_results.name: KleinerLott.IsKappaNoncollapsedOnScale
existing_results.hypotheses: flow : RicciFlowData M; n : Nat; T kappa rho : Real. For every x0 t0 r with 0 < r < rho, r^2 ≤ t0 < T, if HasCurvatureBoundOnParabolicBall x0 t0 r (r⁻¹)^2 then kappa * r^n ≤ volume t0 (ball t0 x0 r).
existing_results.note: Scalar RicciFlowData predicate. No completeness, nonnegativity, or ancient-time hypotheses. Not a kappa-solution.

candidate_tasks.title: Kappa-solution predicate on an existing smooth complete Ricci flow
candidate_tasks.proposed_Lean_statement_or_precise_contr: Define a Prop-valued structure, e.g. KleinerLott.IsKappaSolution or MorganTianLib.IsKappaSolution, on an existing flow object (prefer KleinerLott.SmoothCompleteRicciFlowOn (Iic 0) with toFlowData, or MorganTianLib.IsRicciFlowOn g (Iic 0)). Fields, all explicit: 0 < kappa; connectedness; every time-slice complete (already in SmoothCompleteRicciFlowOn.complete); nonflat (scalar curvature not identically zero on some slice); HasNonnegativeCurvatureOperator of the slice curvature form at every (p,t); a quantitative |Rm|-bound on every slice once curvature-operator-norm exists; IsKappaNoncollapsedOnScale flow.toFlowData (finrank E) T kappa rho for every finite rho (T covering the ancient interval). Do not include roundness, shrinker classification, soul, or canonical-neighborhood alternatives.
missing_dependencies: nonflat predicate on a Ricci-flow family
adapter identifying MorganTian ricciTensorAt / curvature form with KleinerLott.RiemannCurvatureFamily

candidate_tasks.title: C^∞ Gaussian-coordinate compactness of curvature-bounded balls
candidate_tasks.proposed_Lean_statement_or_precise_contr: Source contract (blueprint lem:gaussian-coordinates-convergence, not a Lean theorem): given n-dimensional metric balls (B_k, h_k) of common radius r, covariant curvature bounds |∇^ℓ Rm(h_k)| ≤ C(ℓ) on each B_k, and the exponential map at the center a diffeomorphism from the tangent ball of radius r onto B_k, after isometric identification of the tangent spaces with Euclidean n-space the pulled-back metrics on the Euclidean ball subconverge in the C^∞ topology uniformly on compact subsets. This is the local Riemannian producer that Ch05.Foundations explicitly deferred; it does not assume Hamilton compactness or kappa-solutions. Do not wrap the C^∞ limit into a HasGeometricLimit hypothesis.
missing_dependencies: C^∞ topology / Arzela–Ascoli on RiemannianMetric over a Euclidean ball
uniform C^ℓ bounds on metric coefficients in Gaussian coordinates from |∇^ℓ Rm| bounds
thm:volume-injectivity-radius if one wants to discharge the exp-diffeomorphism hypothesis from volume+curvature rather than assume it

candidate_tasks.title: Restrict an evolving epsilon-neck of depth at least one to a strong epsilon-neck
candidate_tasks.proposed_Lean_statement_or_precise_contr: theorem EvolvingEpsilonNeck.toStrongEpsilonNeck {epsilon : ℝ} {g : ℝ → RiemannianMetric I M} {J : Set ℝ} {x : M} {t0 : J} {tau : ℝ} (N : EvolvingEpsilonNeck epsilon g J x t0 tau) (htau : 1 ≤ tau) : StrongEpsilonNeck epsilon g J x t0. Construction: restrict referenceMetricFamily and normalizedMetricFamily along the inclusion evolvingEpsilonNeckTimeSet 1 ⊆ evolvingEpsilonNeckTimeSet tau (Ioc (-1) 0 ⊆ Ioc (-tau) 0); inherit flow, centralNeck, pullback identity, standard-cylinder identity, and EpsilonCloseFamily (quantified over the smaller parameter type). This is the truncation step in lem:canonical-neighborhood-stability(2). It does not assume caps, C-components, or kappa-solutions.
